home.title: An index of pictographic quality
home.lead: PICTOS Index evaluates each pictogram in its own right, across six dimensions, and as part of a curated AAC library, attending to the formal coherence and visual grammar of the set. The result is a profile for each pictogram; the average currently computed is provisional and has not been validated.
home.privacy: Evaluation data are stored in this browser and exported only when the evaluator chooses.
home.modesTitle: On your own or with a panel
home.soloBody: You review a library by yourself: you interpret each pictogram, rate its six dimensions and download a report.
home.panelBody: To study a library with a group: each person answers on their phone via a QR code, and then two or more judges code their answers.

how.title: Four stages of evaluation
how.loadTitle: Look at the library as a whole
how.loadBody: The whole library is viewed without phrases, and its formal coherence and visual grammar are rated.
how.relationBody: The evaluator’s relationship with AAC is recorded, so each judgement can be read from that experience.
how.evaluateBody: Each pictogram is interpreted without its phrase, and its six dimensions are then rated from 1 to 5.
how.submitBody: The report or the data are downloaded. In a panel, the file downloads by itself and goes to the coordinator.

principles.title: Legibility is necessary, but not sufficient.
principles.body: A pictogram may be easily recognised and still misrepresent its referent, exclude some of its users or sit outside their cultural context. The index therefore integrates communicative effectiveness, cognitive accessibility, cultural adequacy and formal quality, and examines each pictogram both in isolation and within the system to which it belongs.

about.title: An open instrument for pictographic evaluation
about.whatBody: An instrument for evaluating AAC pictograms and libraries: a free interpretation, a six-dimension rubric and an assessment of the set. As generative models produce ever more pictograms, it leaves judgement about their quality to those who use, support or design them.
about.originBefore: It originates in the doctoral research of
about.originAfter: on design for Augmentative and Alternative Communication at Auckland University of Technology (AUT). It is the evaluative counterpart to PICTOS.net, which generates the pictograms, and replaces VCSCI, its first formulation.
about.custodyBefore: It is in the custody of
about.custodyAfter: , a Valparaíso initiative that develops and safeguards open tools for human communication. The code is under the Apache 2.0 licence and the rubric under CC BY 4.0: both may be studied, used, replicated and modified.
about.netBody: It generates pictograms for AAC from a phrase and its context of use. Before drawing, it reasons about what the phrase means; it then composes the image and delivers it as an accessible SVG. PICTOS Index evaluates what PICTOS.net produces.
about.schemasTitle: The schemas of the generative process
about.schemasIntro: The PICTOS.net process moves through three phases, and each one is fixed in a formal schema: a contract the next phase can verify.
about.schemaNlu: the formal understanding of the phrase’s communicative intent, based on NSM and FrameNet.
about.schemaComposition: the structure of the visual candidates, setting a semantic correspondence between word and image.
about.schemaSvg: the SVG as the source of truth: it holds its whole generative lineage and serves both as accessible code and as visual support.

pdf.title: PICTOS Index
pdf.prototypeNote: This index is a prototype under development. Its results are experimental and do not replace comprehension studies or validation with users.
pdf.separateNote: Coherence and grammar describe the library and remain separate from the PICTOS Index average.

clarity.name: Clarity
clarity.description: Clarity is the degree to which the pictogram is visually legible and free from ambiguity.

recognizability.name: Recognisability
recognizability.description: Recognisability is how easily a person can identify what the pictogram represents without additional context.

semantic_transparency.name: Semantic transparency
semantic_transparency.description: Semantic transparency is the degree to which the pictogram accurately communicates the meaning of the target phrase.

pragmatic_fit.name: Pragmatic fit
pragmatic_fit.description: Pragmatic fit is the usefulness of the pictogram in real-world AAC communication situations.

cultural_adequacy.name: Cultural adequacy
cultural_adequacy.description: Cultural adequacy is the relevance of the pictogram to the cultural and linguistic context of its intended audience.

cognitive_accessibility.name: Cognitive accessibility
cognitive_accessibility.description: Cognitive accessibility is how easily people with different cognitive abilities can understand and use the pictogram.

coordination.title: Coordinate a panel
coordination.lead: Here you prepare an evaluation panel: choose the library, give each person a link and, at the end, gather their answers. Everything happens in this browser.
coordination.step1Title: 1. Choose the library and hand out the links
coordination.evaluations: Evaluations downloaded by each person (JSON, you can choose several)
coordination.evaluationsSummary: {n} evaluations: {a} with form A and {b} with form B. {answers} interpretations to code.
coordination.useAgreement: Agreement on “Does it work here?” (Krippendorff’s ordinal alpha; “I cannot judge” counts as missing): {alpha}.
coordination.instructionsBody: Compare each answer with the source phrase and write a number from 1 to 6 in the “codigo” column. Do not look at the other judges’ codes. Save the file as CSV, with the same name.
coordination.code1: Correct: the answer matches the assigned meaning.
coordination.code2: Almost correct: the answer is similar or close to the meaning.
coordination.code3: Doubtful: the answer points to another interpretation or is ambiguous.
coordination.code4: Incorrect: the answer does not match the meaning.
coordination.code5: Opposite meaning: the answer points to the contrary meaning.
coordination.code6: No answer: no answer is given, or the person says they do not know.
coordination.schemeSource: Six-value scheme of Ramírez (2018, p. 80), internally called “Brugger–Frascara”.
coordination.sheets: Coded sheets (CSV, choose all of them)
coordination.needTwoSheets: At least two sheets are needed to compute agreement.
coordination.sheetsUnreadable: The sheets could not be read. Check that they are saved as CSV.
coordination.codingSummary: {judges} judges. Agreement between judges (Krippendorff's nominal alpha): {alpha}. Answers with disagreement: {disagreements}.
coordination.firstRound: Reliability, first complete round (fixed): alpha {alpha}. This upload is round {round}; an alpha after reconciliation measures convergence, not reliability. Report the first-round one.
coordination.howPrivacy: There is no server and no database: the answers go straight from each person to you.
coordination.publishedLibrary: Another library, published on the internet
coordination.libraryUrl: Public address of the JSON file
coordination.badUrl: That address is not valid. It must start with https://
coordination.unreachable: The file could not be read from that address. Check that it is public and serves the file itself, not a preview (see “Where do I publish my library?”).
coordination.notALibrary: The file does not look like a library exported from PICTOS.net.
coordination.whereTitle: Where do I publish my library?
coordination.where1: The address must serve **the JSON file itself**, not a page showing it, and allow other pages to read it.
coordination.where2: **Works:** a GitHub repository (open the file and use the “Raw” button) or a GitHub Gist.
coordination.where3: **Does not work:** Google Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive, because they show a preview instead of the file.
coordination.where4: **Do not change the file** while the panel runs: if it changes, the evaluations can no longer be compared. On GitHub, use the address of a specific commit.
coordination.where5: A library is several megabytes (the sample ones, about 20 MB). To evaluate on a phone, Wi-Fi is advisable.
coordination.linksReady: Give each person their card or their link. Odd numbers answer form A and even numbers form B, so handing them out in order balances the forms.
coordination.linksLocalFile: With a file from this computer the links cannot carry the library: each person will have to load this same file. To avoid that, publish it on the internet.
coordination.cardHint: **Scan the code with your phone’s camera**, or open the link on a computer.
coordination.rolesIntro: A panel involves **two groups of people**, at different moments:
coordination.roleEvaluatorsBody: They answer the instrument, each on their own phone or computer. They write what they think each pictogram communicates and say whether it works in a situation. At least 8 is advisable.
coordination.roleJudgesBody: They come in afterwards. They read the written answers and decide, against the real phrase, whether each one got it right. There are 2 or more, they work separately and do not evaluate pictograms.
coordination.whyJudges: Why judges? Interpretations are free text: someone has to decide whether “I want water” matches “I am thirsty”. With two or more independent judges, it is possible to measure whether that decision is reliable.
coordination.seq1: **You choose the library** and how many people will evaluate (step 1, below).
coordination.seq2: **You hand out a card with a QR code**, or a link, to each person. The link already carries the library.
coordination.seq3: **Each person evaluates** at their own pace. At the end, their phone downloads a file with their answers and they send it to you.
coordination.seq4: **You load those files** (step 2). The screen prepares a sheet for each judge with all the written answers, in random order and without names.
coordination.seq5: **Each judge codes**, on their own, every answer with a number from 1 to 6 and sends their sheet back.
coordination.seq6: **You load the sheets** (step 3) and see how far the judges agree, which answers are worth reviewing together and the results for each pictogram.
coordination.linksPlaceholder: The QR code cards, one per person, will appear here as soon as you choose the library.

set.title: Look at the set
set.intro: Before seeing each pictogram on its own, look at them all together and answer two questions about the set.

notice.start: You will see the pictograms one at a time. For each one, first write what you think it communicates. Then you will see its phrase and answer six short questions.
notice.blind: Part one. You will see pictograms without their phrase. Write what you think each one communicates; if you do not know, say so and move on.
notice.sighted: Part two. Now you will see other pictograms, each with the phrase it means to say. You will say whether it works in that situation.

done.title: You have finished
done.intro: Download the PDF report or the JSON data. Your answers also stay saved in this browser.
done.introProtocol: Send that JSON file to the panel coordinator. Nothing else is needed. If you cannot find it, download it again with the button.
done.downloaded: ✓ Your answers have been downloaded to your downloads folder as “{file}”.
